x: Article 368, in Part XX, gives Parliament the power to amend the Constitution and sets the procedure. Article 356 is President's Rule and 280 the Finance Commission.
t: Recall Article 368 and Part XX.

x: Option D is incorrect: an amendment bill can start only in Parliament, in either House, never in a State Legislature. No prior recommendation of the President is needed.
t: Recall where an amendment bill can start.

x: Both are true: an amendment bill must pass each House separately by special majority, and R defines that majority (a majority of total membership plus two-thirds present and voting). R explains A.
t: Recall the two parts of a special majority.

x: A is false: there is no joint sitting on an amendment bill. B is true: if one House rejects it, the bill fails.
t: Recall that amendment bills have no joint sitting.

x: The 1st Amendment added the 9th Schedule, the 52nd the 10th, the 73rd the 11th, and the 74th the 12th. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall which amendment added each Schedule.

x: I and III are correct: federal provisions need ratification by at least half the States. II is false because not all States must ratify, and IV is false because the President's qualifications and tenure need no ratification.
t: Find the matter wrongly said to need ratification.

x: The President must assent to an amendment bill and cannot veto or return it. The 24th Amendment (1971) made assent compulsory.
t: Recall the 24th Amendment's rule on assent.

x: Option C is incorrect: ratification needs only half the States, by simple majority in each, not all of them. The first amendment that needed it was the 3rd (1954), on Entry 33 of the Concurrent List.
t: Recall that half the States must ratify.

x: The 24th made Presidential assent compulsory, the 26th abolished privy purses, the 44th removed property from fundamental rights, and the 52nd added the anti-defection law. The answer is a-iii, b-i, c-iv, d-ii.
t: Recall each amendment's main change.

x: The 1st Amendment was 1951, the 42nd 1976, the 52nd 1985 and the 73rd 1992. The order is B, A, D, C.
t: Recall the years 1951, 1976, 1985 and 1992.

x: Both are true: the 44th Amendment replaced 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion', and it also let the President return ministerial advice once. Two separate changes do not explain each other, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether two changes in the same amendment explain each other.

x: The 91st Amendment (2003) capped the Council of Ministers at 15% of the Lok Sabha or Assembly.
t: Recall the 15% cap.

x: Both are true: the 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 21A, free education for ages 6–14. The 93rd (2005) added Article 15(5), allowing OBC reservation in educational institutions.
t: Pair the 86th with Article 21A and the 93rd with 15(5).

x: All four are correct: the 26th abolished privy purses, the 61st lowered the voting age to 18, the 69th made Delhi the National Capital Territory, and the 84th froze seat readjustment until 2026.
t: Recall each amendment's main change.

x: Option C is incorrect: the 13th Amendment's Article 371A is for Nagaland, not Arunachal Pradesh. The 89th split the SC/ST Commission, the 83rd exempted Arunachal from SC Panchayat quotas, and the 105th restored States' power to list SEBCs.
t: Recall that Article 371A is for Nagaland.

x: Both are true: the amendment process is partly flexible and partly rigid, and some changes, such as under Articles 3 and 169, need only a simple majority outside Article 368.
t: Recall the three ways to amend the Constitution.

x: New or altered States come under Article 3, creating or abolishing Councils under 169, and judges' salaries can be changed by simple majority. Article 368 amendments need a special majority. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Match each change to its procedure.

x: All seven are federal provisions needing ratification by half the States: Presidential elections, Union-State executive and legislative relations, the higher courts, the Seventh Schedule, Article 368 itself and the GST Council.
t: Recall the federal provisions that need ratification.

x: The 1st Amendment added Articles 31A, 31B and 15(4), and protected land-reform laws from judicial review. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall what the 1st Amendment added.

x: Both are true: the 24th Amendment (1971), passed after Golaknath, confirmed Parliament's power to amend any part, including fundamental rights.
t: Recall the 24th Amendment's response to Golaknath.

x: All four are correct: the 42nd Amendment, the 'mini-Constitution' (1976), added 'socialist', 'secular' and 'integrity' to the Preamble and Part IV-A (Article 51A).
t: Recall the 42nd Amendment's main additions.

x: The 42nd Amendment added the 10 fundamental duties, the Directive Principles in Articles 39A and 43A, moved education to the Concurrent List, and added Part XIV-A. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.
t: Recall the 42nd Amendment's additions.

x: Both are true: the 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from fundamental rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.
t: Recall Article 300A.

x: All four are correct: the 52nd Amendment changed Articles 101, 102, 190 and 191, the 61st (1988–89) changed Article 326, and the 69th (1991) added Article 239AA for Delhi.
t: Recall the Articles each amendment changed.

x: Seven belong to the 73rd Amendment: constitutional status for Panchayats, Part IX (Articles 243–243O), the 11th Schedule (29 subjects), one-third for women, and State Finance and Election Commissions. Municipalities came with the 74th.
t: Find the item that belongs to the 74th Amendment.

x: The 74th Amendment (1992) gave municipalities constitutional status, added Part IX-A (Articles 243P–243ZG) and the 12th Schedule with 18 subjects. The answer is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.
t: Recall the 74th Amendment's parts.

x: All three are correct: the 86th Amendment changed Article 45 and added Article 51A(k), the 11th fundamental duty on parents to educate children.
t: Recall the 86th Amendment's three changes.

x: The 91st (2003) barred defectors from becoming Ministers, the 97th (2011) dealt with co-operatives, the 100th (2015) gave effect to the Bangladesh land boundary deal, and the 101st (2016) brought GST. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall each amendment's year and subject.

x: Both are true: the 99th Amendment (2014) created the NJAC, and the Supreme Court struck it down in 2015. A later strike-down does not explain an earlier creation, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a later event explains an earlier one.

x: All three are correct: the 42nd Amendment (1976) added Part IV-A, whose only Article, 51A, lists the fundamental duties.
t: Recall Part IV-A and Article 51A.

x: The 12th Schedule lists 18 municipal subjects, and Part IX-A, added by the 74th Amendment in 1992, covers municipalities in Articles 243P–243ZG. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the 74th Amendment's parts.

x: A is true: the 42nd Amendment made ministerial advice binding on the President. R is false because the 44th, not the 42nd, let the President return advice once.
t: Discriminate the 42nd Amendment (binding) from the 44th (return once).

x: Both are true: the 9th Schedule, added by the 1st Amendment, protects listed Acts, mainly land-reform laws, from challenge.
t: Recall what the 9th Schedule protects.

x: The 10th Schedule, added by the 52nd Amendment (1985), contains the anti-defection law. The 9th is land reform, the 11th Panchayats and the 12th municipalities.
t: Recall which amendment added each Schedule.

x: Both are true: the 52nd Amendment brought in disqualification for defection, and the 91st barred defectors from becoming Ministers. A later amendment cannot explain an earlier one, so R does not explain A.
t: Ask whether a later amendment explains an earlier one.

x: The 11th Schedule lists 29 subjects for Panchayats. The 12th lists 18 for municipalities.
t: Pair the 11th Schedule (29) with the 12th (18).

x: The 84th Amendment was 2001, the 86th 2002, the 89th 2003 and the 93rd 2005–06. The answer is a-i, b-ii, c-iii, d-iv.
t: Recall the years of the 2000s amendments.

x: All five are correct: the 1st Amendment added the 9th Schedule in 1951, Part IX-B covers co-operatives, the 86th made education for 6–14 a fundamental right (Article 21A), and the 93rd allowed OBC reservation in higher education.
t: Recall each amendment's main change.

x: The 97th Amendment (2011) added the right to form co-operative societies to Article 19(1)(c), along with Article 43B and Part IX-B.
t: Recall the 97th Amendment.
